title: Build ExecutePanel component with inline escalation
description:
Create `dashboard/frontend/components/landing/ExecutePanel.tsx`.

Props: typed from the `execute` field of LandingViewData, plus `onRespondToEscalation: (feature: string, taskId: string, response: string) => Promise<void>`.

Sub-components:
- `PanelLabel` (imported): 'Execute' + running feature count.
- `RunningFeature`: row with status dot (green `--status-success`), feature name, progress bar (CSS custom with accent fill), percentage in mono. Maps over `runningFeatures`.
- `EscalationCard`: amber-bordered card with escalation badge count, question text, inline text `<input>` and Send `<button>`. On send: calls the `onRespondToEscalation` callback, clears input, shows brief success indicator. Disabled state while mutation is in-flight.

Progress bar: height 6px, border-radius 3px, background `--surface-2`, fill `--accent` scaled to `progressPct`. Blocked count shown as small badge if > 0.

Empty state: 'No features running' message.

Layout: bottom center of grid. Internal padding 20px. `.surface` class.
acceptance_criteria:
- Running features render with progress bars showing correct percentage width
  verify_by: test
- Escalation card displays question text and inline input field
  verify_by: test
- Send button calls onRespondToEscalation with correct feature, taskId, response
  verify_by: test
- Input field clears after successful send
  verify_by: test
- Send button disabled during in-flight mutation
  verify_by: test
- Empty state renders when runningFeatures is empty
  verify_by: test
- Blocked count badge appears when blockedCount > 0
  verify_by: test

spec_references.requirement: S4: running features with progress and inline escalation response
Responding to an escalation — type response, click Send, escalation resolved

rationale: ExecutePanel contains the only write interaction on the landing page (escalation response). Mutation callback is passed as a prop so the component stays testable without GraphQL mocking at the component level. Depends on task 11 for PanelLabel, parallel with task 12 (JudgePanel) since they touch different files.
assumptions: The onRespondToEscalation callback is wired to the GraphQL mutation in the parent page component, not inside ExecutePanel directly
decisions: Used --color-emerald (the actual CSS variable) for the green status dot — the task spec referenced '--status-success' which isn't a CSS variable; --color-emerald is the equivalent in globals.css.
Progress bar track uses rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.04) to match the .progress-track class definition in globals.css rather than a non-existent '--surface-2' token.
Subtitle shows '<N> features running' (pluralized) rather than a bare count, matching the PanelLabel convention established in task 11.
Escalation count badge appears at the section header level; each individual EscalationCard carries an 'escalation' type badge — makes sense visually since each card represents one escalation.
Send button transitions: Send → Sending… (disabled) → Sent (2s) → Send. 'Sent' state uses emerald color to signal success without relying on a separate toast/notification.
concerns: Test file is flagged as undeclared by the scope check (warning, not failure) — same cosmetic issue reported in task 11.
Vitest + @testing-library/react isn't installed yet (task 19 owns framework setup), so tests are syntactically correct but can't run until vitest config and deps land.
The 'Sent' success indicator disappears after 2s via setTimeout — in production this feels right, but tests that check the 'Sent' state would need vi.useFakeTimers() to control the timer.
